newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola falls to new lows on commercials, hedge.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola falls to new lows on commercials, hedge.

text.p: WCE canola futures traded down at new contract lows in all months by midsession as prices fell to or near the expanded C$15 a tonne limit on commercial and hedge selling, traders said.
"We're catching up with Chicago's fall Tuesday," a trader said. "Commercials are selling, there's hedges, RBC-DS is buying July and Cargill is buying November."
The WCE was closed Tuesday to mark Canada Day. July WCE futures crush margin fell to -3.26 Wednesday from +0.03 Monday. July-Aug spread from $8 to $10, July-Oct $4. Lows were set in all months.
July fell C$10 to the new low of $362 at 1100 CDT, August fell $12.80 to a new low of $352.10.

July flax fell $5.60 to a new low of $323.50, September sank $4.10 to a new low of $291.30 and November fell $5.70 to set a new low of $286.50 on commercial selling and hedges. RBC-DS bought 100 July-Sep at $30. Peas did not trade.
July western barley lost $1.10 to $121.10 after it set a new low of $120.90 on long liquidation, October lost $1.10 to $125.50 after it set a new low of $125.10 on hedges.
July feed wheat slipped $0.50 to a low of $147.60 on liquidation.
October fell $1.50 to a new low of $151.80 as locals sold to commercials and commission houses.
RBC bought five October oats contracts unchange at US$107.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas.)
